summary: A resource observation seals its latest-state claims (observer.observed, resource.observed and the like) in a batch apart from the messages and subscription claims it writes, so a trim can later delete the observation's envelope whole; a mission request still travels with the discovery it names

replay.detail: The same claims are written with the same content; only the batch each lands in changes, and an observation that writes only one class still seals one batch. Old batches are untouched.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: No claim kind, field, wire or envelope format changes: a batch may already hold any mix of kinds, so older members admit and relay split batches unchanged. Replicated admission does not require cited evidence to arrive first, and a mission request stays in its discovery's batch because the starting host reads that claim when the request arrives.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting seals observations in one batch again.
